analysis:
Examined all supplied workflow excerpts, documentation patches and file metadata against the indexed threat model and selected T-041 detail. The complete workflow range map identifies comment-only changes; .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml:862-864 now describes routing release-check builds without a requested size when sizes are off. docs/developer/build.md:390-397,589-600,623-628 and changelog.d/ci-build-lanes-routed.md:3-5 describe extending this routing to three build lanes, raising requested macOS jobs from 9 to 12, and accepting the approval's pinned size. A smaller approved runner could delay builds, but this is documented operational risk, not evidence of an exploitable availability regression.
Surrounding workflow behavior retains pinned actions, credential-free checkout, bounded jobs, blocking release/focused checks and the result gate (provider-tests.yml:1152-1199); GPU tests remain non-blocking. No supplied executable change weakens provider authorization, encryption, cache isolation, billing or artifact qualification (A-011/A-017, T-054, T-041).
Integration must examine provider-plan.yml and the routing implementation: verify approved runner selection and fallback, lane caps/job counts, and the trust/isolation contract for runners now producing reusable build/test artifacts consumed by provider-ci-products (workflow:740-745,927-971). Those implementations and the build-product producer are absent here, so neither runner compromise nor safe artifact provenance can be established from the documentation. No independently supported finding in this source scope; routing and artifact-trust uncertainty remains material to the combined PR.
